samples.summary: Reverting the CLI login nonce re-opens the loopback callback to any code a browser page pushes at it

finding.summary: Reverting the CLI login nonce re-opens the loopback callback to any code a browser page pushes at it
finding.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:158-190 — startCallbackServer() now resolves on the first `GET /callback?code=…` with no binding check; the backend redirect at packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:127-129 no longer carries `state`, and CliAuthStore no longer stores a nonce (packages/backend/src/auth/cli-auth.store.ts:4-15). The CLI listener's port is guessable and any page in the user's browser can navigate to it, so a code minted by an attacker's own OAuth flow is redeemed by the terminal and saved as the session (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:56-138). Both ends were reverted together, so no caller is left type-broken — the blast radius is that the previously-guarded login path is reachable again. Security-design specifics belong to the security lens; flagged here because the delta makes an older unguarded path live.

verdict.reason: The described behaviour exists (login.ts:168-227 resolves on any GET /callback?code with no binding; auth.controller.ts:127-129 redirects with only `code`), but it is not a blast-radius defect. Grepping every reference to the changed contract shows no off-diff site broken or bypassing: `startCallbackServer`/`waitForCallback` are module-local with a single caller in the same file (login.ts:33,50) and no other reference in packages/cli; the only consumer of the redirect shape is that CLI, and the backend spec (auth.controller.spec.ts:205-209) plus design docs (docs/design/cli.md:180, docs/design/rest-api.md:341) already describe the no-state form, so nothing is stale or type-broken. No surviving guard has a reachable bypass either — the OAuth state guard that does exist (github-auth.guard.ts:21-26 -> github.strategy.ts:59 -> auth.controller.ts:119-137) is traversed by every path through githubAuthCallback; the complaint is that a loopback binding check does not exist at all, which is auth/security-design and explicitly deferred by this lens ("Whether the new guard is the right security design, or auth specifics. That is the security lens. You only care that something bypasses it."). The finding also concedes no caller is left broken, and its cited evidence is partly wrong: CliAuthStore does store a csrf nonce per state (cli-auth.store.ts:4-9,25-34,46); it is merely never forwarded to the loopback. Refuting drops it from this gate only; the security lens retains the substance.

mergedFrom.summary: New CLI + older backend = `wafflebase login` can never complete (version skew across independently released packages)

finding.summary: New CLI hard-requires a `state` echo that older backends never send — version skew breaks `wafflebase login` against any deployed/self-hosted server that predates the backend half of this change
finding.evidence: `startCallbackServer` now rejects (400 "Invalid state") every callback whose `state` does not match the minted nonce (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:206). The echo is produced only by the new `stateEcho` in packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:127-134. The CLI ships to users independently of the server (packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:42, packages/backend/README.md:389 describe self-hosted backends), so a user on the new CLI + an unpatched backend gets a genuine callback with no `state`, sees "Invalid state" in the browser, and the CLI hangs until the 30s timeout with no diagnostic. There is no version negotiation or capability check anywhere in the login flow (login.ts:33-63). Fix belongs on the new CLI code (a clear error naming the server-version mismatch, or a documented minimum server version).

verdict.reason: The described code does not exist in this repository, on either side of the claimed contract. CLI: packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts has no state/nonce handling at all — a grep for 'state' within that file returns zero matches, and startCallbackServer (login.ts:153-270) validates only the presence of 'code', replying 400 'Missing code' (login.ts:178-182) and otherwise resolving with the code (login.ts:223-226). There is no 400 'Invalid state' branch; the cited login.ts:206 is a CSS rule inside the success HTML page. Repo-wide grep for the literal 'Invalid state' matches only stale review artifacts under .agent-review/, never source. Backend: the cited auth.controller.ts:126-136 is the CLI redirect plus the expired-state BadRequestException; the redirect emits '?code=<code>' only (auth.controller.ts:127-129) with no state echo, and grep for 'stateEcho' finds nothing in any source file. There is exactly one CLI login implementation and one definition/caller of startCallbackServer (login.ts:33, login.ts:153), so no alternate variant exists. Because the new CLI imposes no 'state' precondition, an older backend's code-only callback is accepted exactly as before — there is no version-skew break to block on.

finding.summary: `backendErrorEnvelope` discards non-envelope backend bodies, so Nest's default error responses (`{statusCode, message, error:"Not Found"}`) now lose their message on every converted call site
finding.evidence: `backendErrorEnvelope` keeps fields only when `data.error` is a plain object (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:100-107); otherwise it emits just the fallback `HTTP_ERROR` / `HTTP <status>`. The backend has no global exception filter — grep for `ExceptionFilter|useGlobalFilters|APP_FILTER` over packages/backend/src returns nothing, and only docs-content.controller.ts:44 hand-builds `{error:{code,message}}` — so a 401/403/404 arrives as Nest's default `{"statusCode":404,"message":"Document abc not found","error":"Not Found"}`. The passthroughs at packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:202, notes.ts:155, slides.ts:161 still enter their `if (body?.error)` branch (the string "Not Found" is truthy) but now print only `{"error":{"code":"HTTP_ERROR","message":"HTTP 404"}}`, where they previously printed the server's `message` verbatim. Same loss in docs/import.ts:181,217,240, notes/import.ts:170,203,222, slides/import.ts:200,249,268, files/upload.ts:231, files/download.ts:66.

verdict.reason: The finding claims `backendErrorEnvelope` keeps fields only when `data.error` is a plain object and otherwise emits just the fallback, dropping the server message from Nest's default `{statusCode, message, error:"Not Found"}` body. That is not what the code does. At packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:132-136 the message resolves via `messageText(fields.message) ?? messageText(body?.message) ?? messageText(raw) ?? fallback.message` — the second link reads the top-level `message` of Nest's default shape, and the third link reads a bare `error` string. `messageText` (formatter.ts:91-100) also joins ValidationPipe `message` arrays. The fallback `HTTP <status>` is reached only for a body with no text at all. The doc comment at formatter.ts:110-116 states this exact intent. Tests pin it: output.test.ts:273-289 asserts a 404 Nest-default body yields `message: 'Document not found'`; output.test.ts:291-304 asserts array joining; output.test.ts:306-315 asserts `{statusCode:403,error:'Forbidden'}` yields `'Forbidden'`. The converted call sites pass the whole body (e.g. packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:196-208 passes `body`), so the top-level `message` is available. The reviewer's cited evidence range formatter.ts:100-107 is the tail of `messageText` plus doc comment, not the described field-selection-only logic.
